compression_does_not_raise_success: the measured sparse density sweep (evidence/census_sparse.json) is FLAT in density (CP-95 0.2294-0.2535 over 2^-4..2^-8, 16x records), so record-count gains of the size bought here (0.415 bits) do NOT lift recovery toward the dense arm's 0.4098; the floor is NOT claimed for the sparse pipeline

record_layout_v10h_under_declared.defect: x (32 B) + (a,b) packed into 32 B assumes 128-bit coefficients; production coefficients are scalars mod n (256 bits, 32 B each), so the shipped 72 B layout under-declares the record by 24 B

record_layout_v10i_compressed.b_reconstruction: b is NOT stored: it is replayed from the trail start (trail-id) up to step-index, one priced walk step per replayed position, charged ONLY on candidate matches in the recovery path
record_layout_v10i_compressed.layout: x (32 B) + a (32 B, mod n) + trail-id (4 B) + step-index (4 B)
record_layout_v10i_compressed.recovery_path_charge: b-replay = step_index * 1101 instr per candidate record; at the measured merge rate this is <= 2^-40 of the step total and is charged as a recovery-path row, never inside the per-step price
record_layout_v10i_compressed.why_legal: the record key and the solve both use (x, a, b) with b = trail length mod n; storing the trail position instead of b is exact because the trail is deterministic from its seed

why_sparse: dense records at S = 2^127.63 steps would need 2^61.17 B over the 2^73 B cap
